note: Placeholder vocabulary written to unblock the architecture. Every definition must be reviewed by hand before any client use. See docs/PENDING.md.
rules: No diagnostic labels, severities, or disorder names.
No schema names from the Young Schema Questionnaire.
Plain language a client could read without a glossary.
A code describes something the client does, thinks, or reports, not what it means.

codes.label: Holding something back
codes.definition: The client wanted to say something to a specific person and did not.
codes.example: I wanted to tell her it bothered me and I just said it was fine.
codes.counter_example: Deciding not to bring up a topic because it was not the right time, without any sense of having swallowed something.

codes.label: Looking for reassurance
codes.definition: The client asked, or wanted to ask, someone to confirm they were okay, right, or still liked.
codes.example: I texted him three times to check we were good.
codes.counter_example: Asking a colleague a practical question about a task.

codes.label: Pulling away after friction
codes.definition: After a disagreement or awkward moment, the client went quiet, left, or avoided the person.
codes.example: After the argument I just stopped answering for a few days.
codes.counter_example: Taking an hour to cool down and then coming back to the conversation.

codes.label: Expecting to be turned down
codes.definition: The client predicted that a specific person would reject, dismiss, or be annoyed by them, before anything happened.
codes.example: I already knew she'd think I was being needy, so I didn't ask.
codes.counter_example: Recalling an actual rejection that happened.

codes.label: Taking care of others at own expense
codes.definition: The client did something for someone else while giving up something they needed, and noticed the cost.
codes.example: I drove him to the airport at 5am even though I had my exam that morning.
codes.counter_example: Helping someone without any mention of a cost to themselves.

codes.label: Wanting to be noticed or acknowledged
codes.definition: The client wanted someone to recognize something they did or felt, and it did not happen or they did not ask.
codes.example: Nobody said anything about the presentation and it sat with me all day.
codes.counter_example: Receiving thanks and describing it neutrally.

codes.label: Putting off a task
codes.definition: The client delayed a specific thing they intended to do and names what they did instead.
codes.example: I opened the application tab and closed it again and watched something.
codes.counter_example: Rescheduling a task for a stated practical reason.

codes.label: Reaching for a distraction
codes.definition: The client used an activity, substance, or screen to stop thinking about something specific.
codes.example: I scrolled for two hours so I wouldn't think about the call.
codes.counter_example: Relaxing with a show after a long day, with no feeling being avoided.

codes.label: Avoiding a person
codes.definition: The client steered clear of a specific person, place, or message because of what contact might bring up.
codes.example: I saw his name on my phone and put it face down.
codes.counter_example: Not seeing someone because of schedules.

codes.label: Sitting on a decision
codes.definition: The client left a choice open past the point where they say it needed to be made.
codes.example: I still haven't told them whether I'm coming and the deadline was Friday.
codes.counter_example: Taking time to decide something that has no deadline.

codes.label: Replaying a conversation
codes.definition: The client went over something that was said, repeatedly, after it ended.
codes.example: I kept hearing the way she said 'fine' all evening.
codes.counter_example: Remembering a conversation once to report it.

codes.label: Rehearsing a bad outcome
codes.definition: The client imagined, more than once, a future event going wrong.
codes.example: I've already pictured the interviewer's face when I blank.
codes.counter_example: Planning for a realistic risk with a concrete step.

codes.label: Hard on self after a mistake
codes.definition: After an error, the client reports a sentence or thought directed at themselves that is harsher than the mistake.
codes.example: I sent the wrong file and the first thing I thought was 'of course you did.'
codes.counter_example: Noting a mistake and what to do differently.

codes.label: Friendships
codes.definition: The entry reports a concrete event in a friendship this week.
codes.example: We finally got dinner after a month of cancelling.
codes.counter_example: A general statement about friends with no event.

codes.label: Work or school
codes.definition: The entry reports a concrete event at work or school this week.
codes.example: I got the feedback on the draft and it was better than I expected.
codes.counter_example: A general statement about being busy.

codes.label: Routine and sleep
codes.definition: The entry reports a concrete change in sleep, meals, or daily structure.
codes.example: I've been up past three every night this week.
codes.counter_example: Mentioning being tired without a pattern.

codes.label: Something dropped or picked back up
codes.definition: The client stopped doing, or returned to, an activity they value.
codes.example: I went back to the climbing gym for the first time since September.
codes.counter_example: Trying a new activity once.

codes.label: Wanting something different
codes.definition: The client states a specific way they want things to be different.
codes.example: I want to stop being the one who always texts first.
codes.counter_example: A vague wish for things to be better.

codes.label: Reasons to keep things as they are
codes.definition: The client names what makes the current situation worth keeping, or the change not worth it.
codes.example: If I stop texting first, I'm scared we just stop talking.
codes.counter_example: Listing reasons against a change the client never wanted.

codes.label: Something went well
codes.definition: The client reports a specific thing that went well this week.
codes.example: I asked the question in lecture and it was fine.
codes.counter_example: A generic 'the week was okay.'

codes.label: Something the client did that helped
codes.definition: The client names an action of their own that contributed to something going well.
codes.example: I prepped the night before, which is why the morning wasn't a scramble.
codes.counter_example: Attributing a good outcome entirely to luck or others.

codes.label: Naming a need out loud
codes.definition: The client told someone what they wanted or needed directly.
codes.example: I told my roommate I need the kitchen quiet before 9.
codes.counter_example: Hinting or hoping someone would notice.
